nodes.label: Vibes Page - CRT TV Channel Viewer
nodes.description: The Vibes feature in GooseOS is an ambient TV channel viewer rendered as a Win95-style windowed application. The window title bar reads 'CRT.tv' with standard Win95 minimize/maximize/close controls in the upper right. The entire interface is styled as a retro CRT television set rendered in 3D perspective against a teal/sky-blue gradient background with a green grass strip at the bottom, evoking the classic Windows desktop wallpaper aesthetic. The television is a large tan/beige boxy CRT unit occupying most of the window. The screen displays heavy static/noise with full-spectrum RGB color interference lines running vertically — suggesting an untuned or between-channels TV signal. Faintly visible through the static is ghosted dark content, possibly a previously viewed video frame, giving the impression of a real analog TV struggling to receive a signal. Overlaid on the static in bright green terminal-style text is what appears to be a channel identifier or stream label, partially legible as something like 'cybertv.tv' or similar. The right side panel of the TV body contains the physical controls: a black rotary 'channel' dial (large, prominent, round) and a smaller 'power' button below it, both rendered as 3D skeuomorphic widgets. There are also several small square buttons or indicators stacked vertically to the left of the channel dial, resembling preset channel buttons. The bottom of the GooseOS window shows the Win95-style taskbar with a './start' button in the lower left. The overall visual atmosphere is lo-fi, nostalgic, and glitchy — intentionally evoking the experience of watching late-night cable TV on an old CRT set with poor reception.

nodes.label: CRT Television Skeuomorphic Widget
nodes.description: The central UI element is a photo-realistic or heavily styled illustration of a vintage boxy CRT television set. It features a curved screen displaying static noise, a tan/beige plastic housing, ventilation grille on the right panel, and physical-style controls including a large rotary channel selector dial and a power button. The 3D perspective rendering gives it depth and realism within the flat browser window context.

nodes.label: RGB Static Noise Screen Effect
nodes.description: The TV screen renders full-spectrum RGB vertical static interference lines, simulating an analog CRT television signal with no reception or between channels. The noise pattern uses red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta pixel columns in a dense interference pattern. Ghost imagery is faintly visible beneath the static, suggesting a video stream attempting to load or a lossy/degraded video signal. This serves as the ambient visual content for the Vibes feature.

nodes.label: Channel Rotary Dial Control
nodes.description: A large black circular rotary dial labeled 'channel' on the right side panel of the CRT TV widget. This is an interactive control that likely switches between different ambient stream channels or video feeds in the Vibes feature. It is styled as a physical knob with a 3D appearance, consistent with the skeuomorphic CRT TV design.

nodes.label: Power Button Control
nodes.description: A smaller circular button labeled 'power' located below the channel dial on the right panel of the CRT TV widget. Likely toggles the TV on/off or activates/deactivates the stream playback. Styled to match the physical knob aesthetic of the overall CRT TV design.

nodes.label: Win95 Window Title Bar - CRT.tv
nodes.description: The Vibes feature is presented inside a Win95-style window with a title bar reading 'CRT.tv'. The title bar uses the classic blue gradient style with white text. Standard window control buttons (minimize, maximize, close) appear in the upper right corner, consistent with the GooseOS Win95 desktop theme implemented via window-manager.js.

nodes.label: Green Terminal Channel Label Overlay
nodes.description: Overlaid on the static noise in bright green monospace terminal-style text is a channel name or stream identifier. The text is partially legible through the interference, appearing to read something like 'cybertv.tv' or a similar retro internet/streaming channel name. This overlay reinforces the lo-fi aesthetic and suggests the Vibes feature streams from specific named internet channels or ambient video URLs.

nodes.label: Win95 Desktop Background - Sky and Grass
nodes.description: Visible behind the CRT TV illustration is the GooseOS Win95-style desktop background featuring a teal-to-light-blue sky gradient at the top and a solid green grass strip at the bottom. This is the standard GooseOS desktop wallpaper that appears across the application, providing environmental context for the floating window.

nodes.label: Win95 Taskbar with ./start Button
nodes.description: The bottom of the screenshot shows the GooseOS Win95-style taskbar. The './start' button appears in the lower left, styled in the classic Windows 95 Start button format but with a terminal/Unix aesthetic twist using './' prefix notation, referencing shell command syntax. The taskbar is rendered with the characteristic raised 3D border style of Win95.
